findings.rationale: Artifact-derived authorization is implemented, but its independent issuer is not protected: the root-owned runner imports workspace modules that perform launch, observation, and signing. Those modules are absent from the frozen authority policy and can execute as the authority UID before any trustworthy replay. Consequently the author-controlled path to an apparently valid accepted aggregate remains open.
findings.required_action: Close DG10-C4-AI-027 by freezing and replaying the complete authority implementation and Python runtime outside the workspace before accepting any R0-R2 receipt.
findings.title: Authorization still depends on workspace-controlled issuer code

findings.rationale: Ed25519 verification, pidfd, procfs replay, nonces, fixed roots, and direct pipes are present, but the signing module and its remediation dependency are imported from the workspace and are neither policy-pinned nor root-frozen. Modified dependency code can fabricate observations and invoke the authority-owned key while running under the authority UID.
findings.required_action: Close DG10-C4-AI-027 and add adversarial coverage proving that workspace module substitution cannot launch, attest, sign, or import an AI attempt.
findings.title: Signed AI attempts remain forgeable through an unfrozen dependency closure

findings.rationale: The fixed R3 importer and ledger transition correctly require two signed xhigh primaries, but those signatures inherit the unfrozen authority-code defect. A forged accepted R3 receipt can therefore satisfy the otherwise deep transition replay.
findings.required_action: After closing DG10-C4-AI-027, regenerate R3 authority policy and prove the fixed importer rejects attempts produced with any substituted authority dependency.
findings.title: R3 transition trusts a forgeable signer implementation

findings.rationale: Test-access input binding and one-use consumption are implemented, but the two required AI approvals depend on the same unfrozen signing code. Deep replay cannot distinguish an authority-UID forgery produced by a substituted imported module.
findings.required_action: Close DG10-C4-AI-027 before permitting the test-access importer to mint any approval.
findings.title: Test-access approval remains reachable through forged AI provenance

findings.rationale: The operational manifest and scoring code consistently pin execution identity candidate.4.12 (SHA-256 8ffcac1c...), but the active candidate.4.14 acceptance amendment still declares candidate.4.10. The two identities have different bytes, worker closures, and adapter identities. The preregistration predates results, but the active contract is internally contradictory.
findings.required_action: Issue an append-only successor amendment that names the exact candidate.4.12 execution-identity path and SHA-256 used by the active manifest and scoring gate, then replay the succession chain.
findings.title: Active BFCL amendment points to a superseded execution identity

findings.rationale: Fixed aggregate and stage-receipt paths reject ordinary caller mappings, but an author-influenced authority dependency can produce signatures accepted by that importer. Thus the semantic equivalent of caller-minted R0-R2 receipts remains possible.
findings.required_action: Close DG10-C4-AI-027 and regenerate the fixed aggregate only from attempts produced by the fully frozen authority closure.
findings.title: Caller-equivalent R0-R2 receipts can still be minted through authority dependency substitution

findings.rationale: Fixed protected roots, exact inputs, two threads, and atomic one-use consumption are sound after import, but the approval importer accepts signatures originating from the incomplete authority closure. The prerequisite independent approvals are not unforgeable.
findings.required_action: Close DG10-C4-AI-027, rotate or reprovision the authority, and require newly produced protected test-access attempts.
findings.title: Protected test-access importer inherits the incomplete authority trust boundary

findings.rationale: Completion sites are routed through the bootstrap or post-R3 gates, but the post-R3 gate accepts the fixed R3 aggregate whose signed primaries can be forged through the unfrozen authority modules. A forged accepted R3 state therefore unlocks non-bootstrap completions.
findings.required_action: Close DG10-C4-AI-027 and replay post-R3 authorization from newly signed attempts before enabling any completion boundary.
findings.title: Forged R3 provenance can unlock the post-R3 completion gate

findings.rationale: The authority freezes only run_dg10_candidate4_ai_audit.py, while that runner prepends the repository root to sys.path and imports dg10_ai_provenance.py and dg10_remediation.py. The imported provenance module performs the pinned launch, constructs live observations, reads the private key, and signs the statement. Provisioning neither copies nor pins those modules or the full interpreter/import closure in policy. Workspace substitution before privileged invocation can therefore execute as authority UID and produce a cryptographically valid fabricated attestation; later signature and field replay cannot detect that origin.
findings.required_action: Move the runner and every imported authority module into a root-owned, non-writable, content-addressed authority installation; pin and sign every module plus the interpreter and library closure; launch with isolated import semantics and a fixed sys.path; bind path, hash, UID, GID, and mode in policy and runtime observations; and add tests that substitute each workspace module and prove no signature can be produced.
findings.title: The separate-UID signer imports unfrozen workspace code

findings.rationale: execute_pinned_codex constructs the child environment with dict(os.environ) and adds only the nonce and CODEX_HOME. The policy and signed runtime observations attest only nonce presence, not an allowlisted environment or the absence of secret-bearing and outside-bundle variables. The closed-set and no-environment-secrets boundary is therefore instruction-only rather than fail-closed.
findings.required_action: Construct the Codex environment from a minimal explicit allowlist, remove all inherited variables, bind its canonical representation or digest in policy and signed observations, and add tests rejecting extra variables, secret-like variables, and environment-dependent tool descendants.
findings.title: The audit child inherits an unattested host environment
